title: AGICL Ledger (ACL-1.0)
description: A structural schema for the minimum machine-readable ACL-1.0 reporting format. It encodes the eight components, four classification states, and four evidence tiers, and enforces the one rule JSON Schema can enforce: Tier C/D evidence cannot support a Constructed state (ACL-1.0 §5). It does NOT and cannot verify repeatability, that disqualifiers were checked, or that stated evidence matches its sources — those remain auditor judgments under ACL-1.0. Passing this schema means a ledger is well-formed, not that it is a correct audit. Filename uses the AGICL technical namespace; the published protocol name remains 'ACL-1.0'. See ACL-1.0.md.

$schema.description: Optional editor hint pointing at this schema. Not part of ACL-1.0; permitted so authored ledgers and templates remain valid.

document_status.description: Optional status of this ledger document. 'illustrative' marks a fictional teaching example that is not an audit of any real system.

notes.description: Optional free-text note about the document (e.g. a fictional-example disclaimer). Not part of the audit result.

protocol.description: The instrument and version this ledger was produced under. Fixed for this schema.

system.description: The exact object under audit. A ledger is invalid if the object shifts between components (ACL-1.0 §6.1).

audit_date.description: Date the audit was completed (ISO 8601, YYYY-MM-DD).

auditor.description: Name or organization performing the audit.

sources.description: Optional source register. ACL-1.0 §6.2 requires each claim to be recorded with source and date; this array lets a ledger carry those sources by id so components can reference them.

type.description: Nature of the source. Aligns loosely with evidence tiers but does not itself set the tier.

components.description: The eight components of ACL-1.0. Each must carry a state and a tier (ACL-1.0 §5).

boundary_cases.description: Any component whose classification was contested during audit, with its reasoning (ACL-1.0 §6.7, §7). Required, but may be an empty array when no classification was contested.

access_limits.description: Components the auditor could not test, stated plainly (ACL-1.0 §6.5, §8). Required. For a fully open system this array may be empty, and that empty statement is itself the finding.

tier.description: ACL-1.0 §5 evidence tier. A: independent reproduction, disinterested. B: developer disclosure with reproducible method. C: developer disclosure without reproducible method. D: marketing/demonstration/statement.

basis.description: One-line basis for the finding (ACL-1.0 §8 report format).

sources.description: Optional list of source ids (from the top-level 'sources' register) supporting this finding.

allOf.$comment: ACL-1.0 §4/§5: Tier C and D evidence cannot support Constructed. A state's tier is capped by the best available evidence; Constructed requires Tier A or B.
